line: Chalk writes a popular claim about two characters, wipes it, and traces 射 back three thousand years.
line_cn: 粉笔写下网上的说法，再一擦，把「射」写回三千年前。

camera.expresses: attention on how a character or line is built
camera.serves: a component; a step of a proof; a spelling

camera.move: Slow lateral pan along a line
camera.serves: a timeline; a derivation; a list of cases

camera.move: Pull back to a fixed medium frame
camera.serves: a comparison; a claim and its counter-claim

camera.move: Locked frame while a panel slides
camera.expresses: a page turned in the room's own way
camera.serves: a new chapter; a hidden board

camera.expresses: a jump to another part of the wall

camera.move: Cut on a line crossing a seam
camera.serves: cause and effect; the same part in two places

camera.move: Wide shot of the whole wall
camera.serves: the map of what was learnt

transitions: text blocks are never cut by the frame edge while they are read;
Transitions are hard cuts, a sliding panel or a line across a seam;
labels: Chinese is hand-authored stroke data (centre lines + stroke type per stroke) drawn by the chalk engine, never a font's outline. Every character the topic needs is added to the data and checked against an OFL kai font behind it before shooting (how: §10, New characters).
English on the board is a single-line OFL handwriting font (EMS family) drawn by the same engine; symbols missing from the font (arrows, plus) are drawn as strokes.
On the board: keywords only, one line of Chinese, the next line English, a size smaller.
Sizes at 1080p: big characters 300–450 px; labels ≥ 55 px CJK and ≥ 30 px Latin cap height; small writing gets heavier chalk so no stroke is thinner than 3 px.
motion: 30 fps, continuous (render with --fps 30: core/render/video.mjs defaults to 24).

Chalk speed, measured on our demo: a big character takes about 0.1 s per stroke including the air between strokes (a ten-stroke character about 1 s), labels about 0.04 s per stroke. Writing speeds up rather than making the voice wait, but a big character written much faster than about 0.07 s per stroke stops looking like a hand.

When reading time and chalk speed pinch in a short film, change the words, not the hand. Ways that work (choose per film): fewer and shorter blocks on the board; big characters only for what the lesson tracks, everything else at label size; start a block while the voice is still on the previous line, so it is finished when it is named; write the next block while the last one is still being read in the same frame; hold the frame instead of moving on; make the film longer.
Camera eases in and out (cubic), never bounces except a whip landing.

native_moves.name: Write, wipe, rewrite in place
native_moves.does: The wrong reading is written under its object, wiped with one pass, and the right one written in the same spot from the same camera position.
native_moves.fits: a common misconception in physics; a misremembered date; a sum everybody gets wrong.

native_moves.name: Tracked component in accent chalk
native_moves.does: One part keeps its colour and its height across several forms.
native_moves.fits: a root through a word family; a variable through an equation's rearrangements; a gene through generations.

native_moves.name: Sliding panel reveal
native_moves.does: The front panel slides away to show a clean back board, and can slide back to close the lesson.
native_moves.fits: "but before that…"; the hidden proof; the answer kept back.

native_moves.name: A line that sews two boards
native_moves.does: One accent line runs across the seam to join two places.
native_moves.fits: the same constant in two formulas; a quote and its source; cause and effect.

native_moves.name: Drying wet streak
native_moves.does: The freshly wiped board dries back and reveals what was left untouched.
native_moves.fits: yesterday's question; a note left by a student; a reminder at the corner.

native_moves.name: Second hand
native_moves.does: A different, childlike chalk colour and hand on the same board.
native_moves.fits: a pupil's question; a visitor's comment; a wrong attempt.

native_moves.name: Chalk as a measuring tool
native_moves.does: An accent object laid along a white line and ticked off, so a comparison is shown, not told.
native_moves.fits: a unit's origin; a scale; how many of one thing fit another.

score.note: sparse plucked strings with marimba and pizzicato bass
